plain_description.what: Compares routing that borrows strength from the tree's parent cells against the same borrowing over a k-means hierarchy with exactly the same shape, using cross-validation on TRAIN. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: TREE-BACKOFF found a small gain from using the tree's hierarchy; a k-means hierarchy of the same shape tells whether the gain comes from the tree's content or just from having a hierarchy.
plain_description.information: Shows whether the tree's hierarchy is better for routing than a same-shaped k-means one. Result: done. The k-means hierarchy routed slightly better (0.53 points, range 0.11 to 0.94), so 'the tree and k-means are on par' is refuted and 'the tree's hierarchy routes better' is withdrawn. The size of the difference is below what the test was powered to call, it was measured on the training items the pilot had already seen, and on the unseen evaluation items there was no difference.
